literal: Even forgetting, another's ruin do not plot; if plotted, virtue will plot the plotter's ruin.
translation: Do not plot another's ruin, even through forgetfulness; if you do, Virtue itself will plot your ruin.
modern: மறந்தும் கூடப் பிறருக்குக் கேடு செய்ய நினைக்கக் கூடாது; அப்படி நினைத்தால், நினைத்தவனுடைய அழிவை அறமே நினைத்துச் செய்யும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against harboring thoughts of doing harm to others, even in a moment of forgetfulness or inattention. The key word 'சூழற்க' (do not plot) emphasizes that even the mental act of planning harm is dangerous. If one violates this and plots harm ('சூழின்'), 'அறம்' (Virtue or the moral law of the universe) will actively plot ('சூழம்') the ruin ('கேடு') of that plotter ('சூழ்ந்தவன்'). This personification of Virtue as an active agent that retaliates against evil thoughts highlights the inescapable nature of moral consequences.
